verdict.tagline: A relaxing medieval city builder that grows charmingly chaotic over time.
for_you_if: you want a relaxing and simple city builder
you enjoy managing growing medieval settlements
not_for_you_if: you expect deep diplomacy and complex late-game challenges
you are bothered by performance drops on massive maps

super fun only if there was multiplayer with friends to play together and there was a code to join them but still a great game and non repetitive
This game would be top 10 in my library if they had a multiplayer gamemode. other than that the singleplayer aspect is quite fun

claims.claim: Reviewers note that map sizes are limited and express a desire for bigger islands.

citations.review_text: i love this little gem, however the amount of time ive waited for the larger map update seems pretty stupid, given this game should have had it to begin with, it should take nearly no effort to add bigger maps to the game . this isnt a massive complex game.

UI doesn't seem to fit as neatly in the Steam Deck but on PC it's good other than that the game is as advertised (it's good). Some things I would like to see is a day-night cycle and bigger islands/map.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game is simple and easy to learn with minimal tutorial guidance.

citations.review_text: it takes a little time to understand everything but it is a really fun game to play
very fun and no need to spend allot of time learning. Perfect for people who do not  have allot of time to play

Feels pretty unpolished, no tutorial (though simple enough to pick up). Some building chains are required but blocked in island mode (no way to build a noiria but you're punished for not building bath houses which depend on it).

No real sense of progression besides a surprise congratulatory message when you hit certain population thresholds. It's a cozy game, but one that doesn't really offer much.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as simple to learn, relaxing, and straightforward compared to more complex city builders.

citations.review_text:
I still can't belive how can such a simple (and a bit old) game can be as addictive and entertaining to play as factorio or satisfactory. I play a lot of strategie games too, but among those, this is the perfect for a simple chill and relaxing kingdom builder for the experienced and a great introduction to those dipping their toes into the pool of strategy games.  
  
The few downsides to it is that it can be a bit repetative once you got 15 hours (a bit like the 2 week minecraft phase) and a bit overpriced for the seemingly lack of content (not much varity in late-game stages of a save file) The dlc is a suporter pack, only containing a few alternatie designs for not as important structures, meaning they do not fall in the line of locking crumbs of major features/mechanics into dlcs aiming at a section of the game you would not care about if the crumble would not exist. This is a HUGE plus for the devs from me.  
  
I <3 this game

Extemely fun city builder. 

Something about this game is very calm. I do not use that term lightly. I prefer to play this game without any combat, just city management. It is more satisfying in some ways than Cities: Skylines. For me it is a pleasant experience that l love returning to once in a while. 

Do not come in expecting a detailed colony sim, this isn't paradox. Its a relaxing, high replay value city builder that rewards you if you design cities well.

Its simple enough to not be tiring yet engaging enough that I loose myself for hours in it.
I always come back to this game when I get that "I want to play something but I can't pick something and I'm not overwhelmed by choices".

The music is nice and relaxing, the low poly is nice and smooth. 
Expanding your town, maximising efficiency while still making it look nice., not to mention finally having enough archers and ballistas to kill your first dragon and feed your people from its flesh is... satisfying.
I just love it.

I could not recommend this game enough for those that enjoy city building but aren't looking for Skylines level of complexity.

This is a HUGE plus for the devs from me.  
  
I <3 this game

A relaxing game with a lot of freedom but not that much of a challenge. Fun to play every so often to wind down but not something you can consistently hop on daily without getting bored from the repetitive gameplay loop imo. If you like building castles and watching little people run around doing jobs you'll enjoy it.

Pros: You can build actual working castles with walls, gates, towers, and rain arrows on Viking boats like you’re in a movie. Plus the devs never quit – they’re still dropping free updates years later, which is wild. 

Cons: you kinda see everything the game has to offer in one or two runs. It’s not some 500-hour monster. You build, you defend, you probably die to fire, you start over. But honestly? Starting over is half the fun.

For the price of Brunch you get a kingdom to rule and a 90% chance to watch it burn. It’s cozy, chaotic, and weirdly addictive. Not a hardcore strategy brain-burner, more like “I’ll just play 20 minutes” and then it’s 2am. If you like cute games that suddenly get stressful, this is your thing. Go be king. Just… build some wells first. Trust me.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention encountering minor bugs, such as UI popups requiring clicks offset from the button or carts failing to pick up resources correctly.

citations.review_text: This is a good castle building game and it is extremely fun however it would be nice to have an export from cart only option for the fishmonger and butcher other than that 10/10 and I have noticed that with the carts i have had a bug that makes the carts not pick up the resources it is meant to unless the stock pile or fishmonger has the exact amount of resources.

Been a while since i played it last, atleast half a year i think, but it's a really solid game. Many hours of fun have led me to the decision to write a review and let yall know its a good game. I probably bought the game on sale back in the day but i still think i would buy it for the current price, no discount, 20 Euros. I just wish there was more content. Oh also there were some minor bugs  but those barely impact gameplay. (Unless they were fixed but this game is from 2017 so i dont think so). Fun!

Edit: Wait they have actually been updating the game?! I see now that they are working on making bigger maps which i was actually hoping for. I might be getting back into this some more in the future, see yall.

I absolutely adore this game. It's a simple enough gameplay loop that it's the game I go to when I want to play *something*, but don't have the brain energy for too many micro-decisions. It's not a time waster but it's not demanding. It's the level of sandbox that I crave, something where all my decisions are technically allowed but it's always pretty clear what the goals are and what the path forward is. The music is fairly pleasing, I don't get tired of listening to it after a long play session. I'm not frustrated by the time scaling either, where I've found in other games the top speed is far too slow or where the normal speed is already overwhelming. Flicking between each time scale is always purposeful and the game ticks by at a nice pace on max speed when you just want to see your resource numbers change. The flavour is fun, like each peasant having its own little digestible humorous profile, and having statues for the dragons that visit. 

There are some UI bugs that make it... interesting... to navigate at times, like some UI popups that require me to click next to a button to actually click on the button. But as long as you figure out what to do it's still playable and doesn't do this often. And maybe it's just that I still have more yet to learn about some of the mechanics (stockpiles and transport vehicles) but they never actually seem to work for me/contribute anything to the gameplay. Each time I try something gets stuck, like the peasants are so slow to fill up a dock or stockpile with the resource I want, and it's just easier to let them walk to get the items they need rather than using transporters. So I just filter them out of my islands - it's much easier to finetune the resource management when there's less moving parts, and it still works perfectly fine (as evidenced by managing to get all of the achievements without understanding how to make these work properly). cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight intricate challenges like storage limits and population mechanics, noting severe performance drops on massive saves.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game struggles with optimization, with frame rates dropping significantly on larger saves with thousands of citizens.

citations.review_text: Its a very good game but still needs to be optimzed for slower computers

Great game. Very addictive. Horrible optimisation.

This is a simple, yet very engaging little game. I have been following this game's development for years and it is amazing how far it has come. There is a lot of things you can do and build, but not too overwhelmingly much, and the game's mechanics are easy to grasp and enjoy. However, what has always been a problem in this game is optimisation. Like, REALLY. When the game is running of the components never reach load over 70 percent. So it is not the fault of my gaming rig, we can rule that out. The game, however, runs at 20 fps at BEST. And the further you develop your kingdom, the worse it gets. My saves with 3000 citizens run at LESS THAN 10 FPS. You get used to it fast, and fortunately, it is not a game that requires superduperhigh framerate to enjoy it. But c'mon, less than 10 frames per second is just pitiful. Eyes literally begin to hurt after looking at framerate like this for some time.

The content of the game, as I have previously mentioned, is great, really. That's why, in the end, I still recommend it. But ♥♥♥♥, devs, please optimise your game. After all these years you certainly already should have.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the peasants as lacking a natural reproduction mechanic, meaning the settlement's population relies entirely on immigration.

citations.review_text:
8/10 - Bought on sale and worth it at the reduced price. However, game is now almost 10 years old but seems to have persistent bugs that have seemingly never been addressed. Some are graphical, with destroyed structures persisting on the map until game is reloaded, though this is rare but often confusing. Fishing docks never display held stock and the tooltip for this building is very misleading. Multiple fishing huts are needed to feed a single fishmonger but you are cautioned not to overfish... A trap for new players. On the subject of Butchers and Fishmongers, they are vital to make your pork and fish go further, but also double as THE ONLY STORAGE for same, so you will find yourself exceeding your storage limits for pork and more rarely, fish, constantly. The miserly storage limits are very annoying.

However, game is mostly great fun unless you go for the harder settings in which case you may find it less so. Oddly, the game is happy enough to apply a natural death mechanic for your peasants (they grow old, die, or are killed doing their jobs - drowning, mining accidents, eaten by wolves, but the poor wretches seem unable to reproduce on their own. No babies. Your only source of new peasants is immigration (so, not a game for the red hat wearing cellar dwellers and window lickers). Depending on how happy a place your realm is, and if you have living space to spare, you'll either get immigrants coming in to live, or they'll visit and leave if they don't like what they see. They'll even refuse to settle while Vikings are raiding AND will often be scared off if you defeat said Vikings, deeming your settlement too violent. Yeah, devs are trolls.

All-in-all a great game to sink time into, very satisfying. I should note that game balance is a little off however, mostly when it comes to limited storage capacities and the fact EVERYTHING requires staffing, and that means you need more and more people and you never really have enough unless you turn off some buildings …

-14JAN2026-


This game is incredibly deceptive. It looks like a generic isometric pixel art mobile game, don't let that fool you.

The mechanics are relatively simple, build houses to attract more population, make enough food to support that population and also have enough surplus to make it through the winter, add leisure buildings to keep your population happy, and lastly develop defences to repel the Viking, dragon, and if you are playing with it enabled other kingdoms when they attack you.

You time warp when you play this game, it's kinda like the 'just one more turn' trope from Civ titles, but this one has you prepping for the next Viking invasion.


The game is a big balancing act, you need to be strategic with farm placement, irrigation placement, where housing and entertainment are, plan ahead for fortifying weak points. The biggest thing you have to monitor is job priority, once there are 0 idle citizens other jobs will be prioritised and your population will begin to neglect tasks. I have had many kingdoms stall out and death spiral because the cascading effects of neglecting certain jobs will murder you.



This game is my go to when I don't feel like getting really invested in a game, when I don't know what to play, or while I am waiting for some other game I play to release a major update.

It's surprisingly complex, attempting to get your population as high as possible. However, because it is so casual it is very easy to put down to do something else. I would say this is a perfect casual city management game.


Plus you can make it as easy or as difficult as you want. I personally like to play on Vintar which is the hard mode but there is a more difficult setting where you will fail eventually. There is also a peacful mode where you can just focus on making a cozy kingdom.



If you like city management type games, tower defence, and enjoy optimising logistics you will really enjoy this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that diplomacy options with other kingdoms are shallow and lack depth.

citations.review_text: It's a fun game I like the castle building part of the game. One thing I would improve is the diploecy the traded and contacted to other kingdoms is a little bland. :)

Short Version: Successful, satisfying, and simple city builder. Diplomacy could use some depth. There could be more mechanics geared towards later city development. Overall, would recommend for relaxation and simplicity.

Long Version: This generally is a very relaxing city builder game with a few moments of tension due to viking raids or rogue dragons. I have two primary gripes about this game. Firstly, once you reach a certain level of development there isn't a lot else more to do except more of the same. Second, Diplomacy is very very simple and could benefit from some depth development. That said I usually play this game to relax and it does a very good job of that. It is also incredibly satisfying seeing your city slowly expand and become better defended.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that when citizen idleness hits zero, job priorities shift and cause tasks to be neglected, which can trigger cascading failures and death spirals in the colony.

citations.review_text: This is one of those games that I find myself picking up again and again, year after year. Easy to learn, excellent difficulty curve as your kingdom grows. Keeps it from getting too cozy feeling! Also love the developers attention to the game years after it's been finished.
